stem: A school has 180 students in grade 10, each of whom is either a boy or a girl. Exactly \(\frac{2}{3}\) of the boys and exactly \(\frac{3}{4}\) of the girls went on a field trip, and 128 students went in all. How many girls are in grade 10 at the school?
solution: Let \(b\) and \(g\) be the numbers of boys and girls: \(b + g = 180\) and \(\frac{2}{3}b + \frac{3}{4}g = 128\).
Multiply the second equation by 12: \(8b + 9g = 1{,}536\). Multiply the first by 8: \(8b + 8g = 1{,}440\).
verify:
b, g = symbols('b g')
sol = solve([b + g - 180, Rational(2, 3)*b + Rational(3, 4)*g - 128], [b, g])
assert sol == {b: 84, g: 96}
assert [Rational(s) for s in spr_answers] == [sol[g]]
